textbookText: - **Ideal gas boundary:** holds at **low P, high T**. Deviations increase at **high P, low T** (finite volume + intermolecular attraction). - **Bohr model boundary:** works ONLY for hydrogen-like (one-electron) species; fails for multi-electron atoms, fine structure, Zeeman & Stark effects. - **Rydberg boundary:** the series label depends on the LOWER level (n₁); emission lines only. - **Kinetic theory boundary:** assumes point particles with elastic collisions. Real gases deviate: high P → volume term; low T → attraction term. - **Triple point boundary:** each pure substance has ONE triple point; CO₂'s is above 1 atm so dry ice sublimes at room pressure.
